home.lede: Ankore is a lean Worker module for products that need remembered users, trusted devices, recoverable sessions, API keys, and entitlements without forcing sign-up at the first useful moment.

lifecycle.label: Anonymous subject
lifecycle.text: Start saving product state before sign-up.

lifecycle.label: Trusted device
lifecycle.text: Remember the browser or native app safely.

lifecycle.label: Recoverable session
lifecycle.text: Issue scoped tokens and rotate them cleanly.

lifecycle.label: Optional account
lifecycle.text: Attach email, billing, teams, or API keys later.

problem.title: Most auth systems start with the heaviest question.
problem.copy1: Products often need a stable identity before they need an account. A user may need to save a draft, keep a device trusted, resume a flow, or recover a link long before they care about passwords, billing, teams, or profiles.
problem.copy2: Ankore separates continuity from account management. Begin with an anonymous subject, then attach stronger proof, recovery, ownership, and paid capabilities when the product experience actually asks for them.

why.title: Stop asking for accounts before value exists.
why.intro: Ankore exists for products where “remember me” matters before “sign me up”. It gives teams a stable subject model first, then lets stronger proof attach over time.

reasons.title: Continuity is not the same as account management
reasons.text: A product often needs to remember a person or device before it needs a profile. Ankore keeps that first identity primitive small and portable.

reasons.title: Recovery should be an upgrade, not a gate
reasons.text: Email challenges, account links, and ownership proofs are added when a user wants durability. The first session can stay lightweight.

reasons.title: Product state should survive auth changes
reasons.text: Anonymous usage, recovered access, and account-backed access all point at the same subject instead of forcing data migration between auth modes.

reasons.title: The boundary should be inspectable
reasons.text: A small Worker + D1 module is easier to audit than a broad auth platform. The product decides which capabilities to enable.

architecture.title: A small identity boundary between product code and account features.
architecture.intro: Ankore is intentionally boring: one Worker package, one database binding, typed client helpers, and explicit configuration for origins, secrets, recovery, and rollout.
layers: Calls Ankore client helpers, stores public subject/device identifiers, and owns the product experience.
Validates requests, issues sessions, handles recovery challenges, and exposes the identity API.
Keeps subjects, devices, sessions, accounts, API keys, entitlements, and audit trails.
Email delivery, billing, analytics, and product-specific APIs attach through explicit configuration.

integrations.title: Adopt the parts your product actually needs.
integrations.intro: Ankore is not a replacement for every account system. It is the continuity core that lets product state survive across anonymous, recovered, and account-backed use.

paths.title: Browser products
items: Create or resume a device identity

paths.title: Worker APIs
items: Verify Ankore sessions at API boundaries
Use subject ids as product owners

paths.title: Service access
items: Issue API keys from the same identity core

paths.title: Recovery flows
items: Send challenge emails from a configured provider
Restore access to the original subject
